title: fix(app-shell): read find() results as QueryResult declares them
body:
Fixes #5945

Both app-shell `find()` readers normalised a result with the same chain:

```ts
Array.isArray(res) ? res : res?.records ?? res?.items ?? res?.data ?? [];
```

`QueryResult` (`packages/types/src/data.ts`) declares exactly one rows member —
`data` — alongside `total`, `page`, `pageSize`, `hasMore`, `cursor`, `metadata`.
`records` and `items` are not members of it, and both were tried **before** the
one that is. This reduces each reader to what the contract declares.

## Per-arm producer search — the gate on each deletion

Each arm was measured before removal, not assumed dead.

**`records` — no producer at the `DataSource.find()` seam. Deleted.**
Searched: every `find()` implementation in the repo (`async find(`, plus the
property/arrow forms fakes use), and every object literal building a `records`
key with an array-ish value. `ObjectStackAdapter.normalizeQueryResult`
(`packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts:3246`) reads the server's
`records` / `value` envelope and returns `{ data, total, page, pageSize, hasMore }`
— so the spelling exists only **below** the adapter, on the wire and in the
client SDK. `packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/consoleUserPreferenceBudget.test.tsx`
is the clearest evidence: it fakes `ds.client.data.find` — the SDK beneath the
adapter — and its own comment says "The client SDK answers with `records`, which
is what `normalizeQueryResult` reads". Every other real producer
(`ApiDataSource`, `ValueDataSource`, `mockDataSource`, the REST example, the
gallery/demo sources) returns `data`.

**`items` — no producer at any seam. Deleted.**
Every `items` in the repo is the unrelated UI-schema key (dropdown menus,
timeline, accordion, breadcrumb). Nothing builds an `items` envelope from a
`find()`.

**Bare array — LIVE. Kept.**
This is the arm the card flagged as not automatically removable, and the
measurement says keep it: the fake in this module's own
`AssignedUsersSection.test.tsx` answers `find()` with a plain array
(`rows.filter(...)`), as do many fakes elsewhere. Deleting the guard would have
turned a tidy-up into a defect, so it stays and is pinned alongside the
deletions.

Two `records` readers found nearby are on **different seams** and were left
alone: `marketplaceApi.ts` / `packagedActions.ts` read a raw HTTP payload rather
than a `QueryResult`, and `ViewDataProvider` returns its own `ResolvedData`
interface, which declares `records` legitimately.

## What the branches did with the shape

No silent data loss is reachable today, because no producer emits either key —
so unlike the precedent in this lane, nothing was being discarded in practice.
The latent hazard is the **precedence inversion**: the contract's member was
consulted third, and because `??` only falls through on nullish, a
present-but-empty `records: []` would have short-circuited a populated `data`.
That is the shape worth removing before a producer ever appears.

## Observable behaviour change

A `find()` answer shaped `{ records: [...] }` or `{ items: [...] }` now reads as
**no rows** at these two seams. Both call sites degrade rather than throw: the
approver directory reports the reference unresolved (falling back to the
prettified machine name, staffing probed-empty) and the assigned-users section
renders its empty state. Spelled out in the changeset.

## Pins, and the red-against-unfixed-source verification

Two new files, each covering all four shapes — the two deleted, the contract
member, and the live bare array:

- `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/useApproverDirectory.contractEnvelope-5945.test.tsx`
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/AssignedUsersSection.contractEnvelope-5945.test.tsx`

Verified red against unfixed source, with the implementation committed first so
the restore leg had a real reference point, and a restore trap on absolute paths:

1. **Fixed tree** — 5 files, `Test Files 5 passed (5)`, `Tests 36 passed (36)`.
2. **Mutated** — the tolerant chain reintroduced in both sources, confirmed *on
   disk* by grep (injected-text count 1 per file, reduced-form count 0), not by
   the editor's exit code.
3. **Pins against unfixed source** — `Test Files 2 failed (2)`,
   `Tests 4 failed | 4 passed (8)`. Exactly the four "does NOT read" pins went
   red while the four positive pins (`data`, bare array) stayed green — the pins
   are specific to the deletion rather than to noise.
4. **Restored** — `git checkout HEAD -- ` on absolute paths, proven by an empty
   `git diff HEAD` plus blob-hash equality against the HEAD blobs
   (`197e1351…`, `df3254ce…`), residual tolerant chains on disk 0.
5. **Pins against restored source** — `Tests 8 passed (8)`.

## Verification

All run at `ac9969bab`, the final commit on this branch.

- Dependency closure built first: `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` — lock verdict `command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` over the two pins plus the three existing suites covering these modules — `Test Files 5 passed (5)`, `Tests 36 passed (36)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` — exit 0. Both new test files are genuinely in the program: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` shows 1 hit each of 4483 files, so "typecheck clean" actually covers them.
- Gate family derived from this repo's own `package.json` and `.github/workflows/` (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` lives in objectstack and only answers for that tree): `check:control-bytes`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `changeset:check`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import` — all exit 0, each printing its own OK line.
- eslint **narrowed to the four changed files**, declared: exit 0, `files linted: 4`, `errors: 0 warnings: 19` (all pre-existing `no-explicit-any` plus one pre-existing `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` at a line this diff does not touch). The narrowing is a measurement, not a skip: population came from eslint's own config resolution (`--print-config` resolves for all four), the count came from `--format json`, and type-aware linting is off (zero `project:` / `projectService` in `eslint.config.js`), so this diff cannot move the verdict of any untouched file. CI runs the full farm regardless.

## Out of scope, filed separately

The producer sweep turned up the same tolerant read on the same seam in about
seven modules this card does not name — `related-count-store.ts` reads `records`
*ahead of* `data`, the same inversion. Recorded as #6726, which stays open and is
not addressed here.
